title: Connected punctured principal slices of excellent normal local rings
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be an excellent Noetherian normal local integral domain of finite dimension at least $3$ [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. For every nonzero $f\in\mathfrak m$, the subspace $V(f)\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is nonempty and connected. Here $V(f)$ is the set of prime ideals containing $f$, with its Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; connected means that it has no decomposition as a union of two disjoint nonempty open and closed subsets.

source.place: Tag 0ECR, lemma-punctured-still-connected, applied to the normal domain completion and the principal ideal (f); descend connectedness along the surjective faithfully flat completion map. Completion normality: More on Algebra, lemma-completion-normal-local-ring (Tag 0C23). This is the connectedness input used in ILO XVII Lemma 3.5.8.

proof.text: Put $B=\widehat A$, $\iota:A\to B$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mB$, and $N=\dim A$. The cited completion statements give: $B$ is Noetherian and local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$; $B/\mathfrak n\cong A/\mathfrak m$, compatibly with $\iota$; $B$ is $\mathfrak n$-adically complete; and $\dim B=N\geq3$. The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated since $A$ is Noetherian, as required by the completion-mod-ideal statement. Its extended ideal is exactly $\mathfrak n$, so that statement gives completeness for the required maximal-ideal topology.

source.place: Tag 07NV, lemma-completion-dimension, and the preceding permanence-of-properties-under-completion paragraph

proof.text: Excellence of $A$ includes the G-ring condition [def-exc-excellent-ring], so [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular], applied with $I=\mathfrak m$, makes $\iota:A\to B$ flat with Noetherian fibre rings $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Taking the trivial extension $\kappa(\mathfrak p)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, each fibre ring is a regular ring, hence a normal ring by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal]. Now $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian (Step 1), $\iota$ is flat, its fibres are normal and $A$ is normal, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-normal-fibres-noetherian-normal] gives that $B$ is a normal ring. By the definition of normal ring, $B_{\mathfrak n}$ is an integrally closed domain. Every element outside the maximal ideal of the local ring $B$ is already a unit, so $B_{\mathfrak n}=B$ under $b/s\mapsto bs^{-1}$. Consequently $B$ is a domain (and is nonzero).

source.place: Tag 0C23, lemma-completion-normal-local-ring, whose proof is Algebra Tag 0C22 (lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian) applied to the completion map, with excellent => G-ring => regular formal fibres

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Because $B$ is a domain, $(0)$ is a prime ideal. Every nonempty basic open $D(b)$ contains $(0)$: if $D(b)$ contains a prime, then $b\ne0$. Hence every nonempty open contains $(0)$. Any two nonempty opens therefore intersect, which proves directly that $X$ is irreducible and that every nonempty open subspace of $X$ is connected. Thus the sole irreducible component is $X$, of dimension $N$. For a proper closed subset $Z$ its complement is a nonempty connected open. For $Z=X$ the complement is empty, hence not connected under the cited convention. The quantities in the connectedness estimate are therefore $d=N$ and $c=N$; here $\dim\operatorname{Spec}B=\dim B$ by the ring-dimension definition.

source.place: Tag 0ECR, lemma-punctured-still-connected: the quantities c and d in the integral-spectrum case

proof.text: Let $g=\iota(f)$ and $I=(g)\subseteq B$. As $f\in\mathfrak m$, we have $g\in\mathfrak n$, and $I$ is proper and generated by one element. The estimate applies to the complete Noetherian local ring $B$ from Steps 1 and 2. Step 3 gives $\min(c,d-1)=N-1\geq2$, so $1<\min(c,d-1)$. Its final assertion yields that $W=V_B(g)\setminus\{\mathfrak n\}$ is nonempty and connected. No normality or excellence of the quotient $B/(g)$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0ECR, lemma-punctured-still-connected, final assertion, with the generator bound Tag 0DX9

proof.text: The completion statement makes $p:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, $\mathfrak q\mapsto\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, surjective. A prime $\mathfrak q$ lies over $\mathfrak m$ only if it contains every $\iota(a)$ for $a\in\mathfrak m$, hence contains $\mathfrak mB=\mathfrak n$ and equals $\mathfrak n$. Conversely $\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak m$ by the residue-field isomorphism of Step 1. Also $g\in\mathfrak q$ if and only if $f\in p(\mathfrak q)$. Consequently $p^{-1}(V_A(f)\setminus\{\mathfrak m\})=W$, and the restricted map $W\to V_A(f)\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 00MC, lemma-completion-faithfully-flat; Tag 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated, and Tag 05GI, lemma-radical-completion

proof.text: The map $p$ is continuous directly from $p^{-1}(D_A(a))=D_B(\iota(a))$; its restriction to the displayed subspaces is therefore continuous. Its target is nonempty since $W$ is nonempty. If the target had a partition into two nonempty open-and-closed subsets, their inverse images would be open and closed, disjoint, cover $W$, and both be nonempty by surjectivity. This contradicts the connectedness of $W$. Thus $V_A(f)\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$ is nonempty and connected, as asserted.
